judged_text: The iframe height is measured exactly once at window.onload and never re-measured, while the iframe is created with scrolling='no'. Posts containing images that load after onload (or any late layout shift) grow the document past the single reported height, and the overflow is permanently clipped with no scrollbar — readers lose the bottom of the discussion on any embed with unsized images.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does measure and post the iframe document height only once (in `app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb` via `window.onload`), and the parent iframe is created with `scrolling = "no"` (`app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`). However, the finding’s core claim—"images that load after onload" causing the reported height to be too small—is not supported by the diff: `window.onload` fires after the iframe document’s resources (including images) have finished loading, and there is no lazy-loading or post-onload DOM mutation shown here that would reliably increase height after the onload measurement. So the specific clipping scenario described isn’t verifiable from the changes shown.
